subject.title: refactor: move non-session runtime journals to SQLite

question: May this refactor intentionally remove the documented ACP `streamLogPath` response and replace file-backed memory artifacts with virtual inline artifacts, or must both contracts receive compatibility transitions?
rationale: Repository policy treats documented responses, plugin APIs, and stored-state upgrades as compatibility-sensitive; source inspection can identify the break but cannot choose whether maintainers intend to accept it.

options.title: Add compatibility transitions
options.body: Keep existing consumers working while introducing explicit SQLite history and discriminated virtual-artifact APIs with documentation, tests, and a removal plan.

options.title: Approve the breaking contracts
options.body: Explicitly accept the upgrade break, document affected integrations and recovery behavior, and require strong live upgrade proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Add compatibility transitions
recommendation.body: Keep existing consumers working while introducing explicit SQLite history and discriminated virtual-artifact APIs with documentation, tests, and a removal plan.

likelyOwner.reason: The adjacent merged SQLite storage work provides the clearest available ownership signal for the database and migration boundary.
